note: Source says shots were fired at the crowd and does not say they came from the house. Other details match: 500 workers, three dead including a child, machine burned on bridge, £250 to Phelps.
Source says a day of '13 to 16 or even 17 hours was not uncommon', not simply 13 to 17. The 7s 6d to 10s wages are the weavers' own estimates.
Figures £3,572 (1857) and £57,720 (1890) match, but the source table is titled 'Analysis of Output of the Bradford Company', not sales. Text says 'sales'.
Source says a plan was made to transfer Avon's general rubber goods to Bradford, gives no date for it, and doesn't say it was carried out. Text says the plan 'moved' production that year.
Source gives '3600 plans' and 'catalogued more than 240 volumes' since mid-January, partial counts of work in progress. Text says 'over 3,600' and 'holds', presenting them as totals.
Source calls Barton Grange a 'manor farm' of Shaftesbury Abbey, not a 'home farm'. Other claims (1330s, 1332 rectory, c.43 m earlier barn c.1300) match.
Source says Malmesbury 'reports that it was standing in the 1120s'; it does not say he saw it. Other claims (1001 grant, early 11th-century build, Edward relics as possibility) match.
